summary: Malta is part of the Schengen Area: EU citizens travel freely, and Swiss and EEA nationals enter with a valid identity card or passport; nationals of the countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806) can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period (ETIAS is not yet in operation), and nationals of the countries on its visa-required list (Annex I) need a Schengen short-stay visa (standard fee €90 under the Visa Code). Malta's Central Visa Unit says the responsibility of issuing visas is shared with Malta's diplomatic missions abroad.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Malta?
faq.answer: EU citizens travel freely, and Swiss and EEA nationals enter with a valid identity card or passport. Nationals of the countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806) can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period (ETIAS is not yet in operation). Nationals of the countries on the EU's visa-required list (Annex I) need a Schengen visa; Malta's Central Visa Unit shares the responsibility of issuing visas with Malta's diplomatic missions abroad.

faq.question: How much does a Malta Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The European Commission lists the Schengen short-stay visa fee as €90 for adults, €45 for children aged 6–12, €35 for applicants from Armenia, Azerbaijan and Belarus and €67.50 for applicants from Cabo Verde. Malta's Long-stay Visa Fees Regulations (L.N. 287 of 2020) set the fee for a long-stay visa at €70 for study purposes and €100 for any other purpose, and long-stay visas are issued free of charge to family members as defined in Malta's free movement order and to minors under six.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Malta?
faq.answer: ETIAS is currently not in operation and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. The official ETIAS website gives the application fee as EUR 20.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Malta without a visa?
faq.answer: Nationals of the countries on the EU's visa-exempt list can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and the UK government tells British visitors that visits to Schengen countries in the 180 days before travel count towards the 90 days.
